NRL Casualty Ward: Panthers' Yeo blow; Ward, Iongi, Tupouniua felled
Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo left the field in the first half at Go Media Stadium on Friday night with a suspected pectoral injury.
Yeo went in to make a tackle and immediately reached for his shoulder and had a shocked look on his face as he reeled away.
The NSW and Australian captain left the field in the 34th minute and cut a forlorn figure on the Panthers bench in the second term. He will be sent for scans to confirm the severity of the injury.
Before the game, Panthers centre Casey McLean had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean saw three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
In Friday's second game, Roosters fullback James Tedesco missed the Round 23 blockbuster against the Bulldogs after failing to overcome an ankle injury.
Tedesco sat out the second half of the Round 22 slaughter of the Cowboys with ice on his ankle but he was initially named to return against the Bulldogs.

"Not sure how bad it is, but he's felt it in the same spot where he injured about eight weeks ago, so not ideal," Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said after the game.
"He's pretty devastated because he was training really well and he was just excited to get back playing, this is what he does, this is what he loves doing, so he's pretty shattered."
The Knights suffered a blow ahead of Sunday's trip to Canberra with star centre Bradman Best dropping out with a calf strain suffered in last week's win over Brisbane.
Manly lost prop Taniela Paseka during the first half in Perth on Saturday with the club reporting he had suffered MCL damage and would be sent for scans on his knee.
The Sea Eagles went into the game without Ethan Bullemor , who s uffered a head knock in training and will follow NRL concussion protocol. He will be stood down for 11 days meaning he will miss this week's clash and next Friday's game against the Dolphins.
The Sea Eagles have also lost back-rower Kobe Hetherington for the remainder of the season after he suffered a ruptured bicep in training on Monday. He will undergo surgery next week.
The Rabbitohs have suffered another injury blow, with Ashton Ward leaving the field with a hamstring injury suffered while kicking for goal in the first half of his side's win over the Eels.
Winger Campbell Graham missed the game with a calf injury suffered in training, which could sideline him for 3-4 weeks.
The Eels also have their own injury worries, with Isaiah Iongi also limping off in the first half. He returned to the bench in the second half pictured in a brace on his right knee.
Eels coach Jason Ryles said post-match there was concern for MCL and PCL injuries, with scans on Monday to confirm to extent of the damage.
Sharks pair KL Iro (concussion) and Siosifa Talakai (biceps) are out of the Round 23 clash against old foes the Dragons.
Titans halfback Zane Harrison has been ruled out for the rest of the season after injuring his hamstring against the Warriors.

Raiders vs Knights Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 23 2026
August 8 th 2026, 2:06am , By: Ben Bridge
Sunday afternoon at GIO Stadium gives us one of the most intriguing price disagreements of Round 23, as Canberra host Newcastle in a match the market has struggled to separate. The Raiders are narrow favourites, but I have the wrong team on top and will back the Knights money line at $2.05.
Newcastle enters after an emphatic 30-6 win over Brisbane, while Canberra was comprehensively beaten 42-18 by Penrith in Mudgee. The Raiders’ previous good form deserves respect, but Newcastle currently possesses the more reliable spine, the stronger recent defensive performance and the greater attacking ceiling.
Money has already arrived for the Knights after they opened at a larger outsider price, and I agree with the move. Newcastle have Kalyn Ponga, Fletcher Sharpe, Bradman Best, Dane Gagai and Dominic Young available, while Tyson Frizell reaches another important career milestone.
Canberra regain Simi Sasagi after injury, but Sebastian Kris is out, and their young halves must recover quickly from a difficult evening against Penrith.
The venue keeps this close. GIO Stadium remains a significant advantage for Canberra, and the Raiders’ middle can make life difficult for any opponent. But at plus money, Newcastle are the side I want.
Raiders vs Knights Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 23
Raiders Brought Back to Earth by Penrith
Canberra entered the Mudgee clash chasing a fifth consecutive win and carrying genuine momentum after a strong month. Penrith brutally halted that run, scoring 42 points and effectively deciding the game through a dominant opening half.
The Raiders had been playing with confidence through Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange and Ethan Sanders, but Penrith prevented the young spine from establishing field position. Canberra’s forwards were forced to work out of their own end, and the defensive line struggled once Nathan Cleary and Isaah Yeo began creating repeated movement.
The loss should not erase the previous improvement. Canberra’s attack had become considerably more dangerous, with Weekes providing speed from fullback and Strange becoming increasingly comfortable running directly at defensive lines. Sanders gives the side an organising half and a strong long kicking option.
The pack remains Canberra’s greatest strength. Joseph Tapine, Corey Horsburgh, Morgan Smithies, Zac Hosking, Ata Mariota, and Josh Papali’i provide power, work rate and experience. If those players win the middle, Canberra can place Newcastle under substantial pressure.
Simi Sasagi’s return strengthens the centres after he missed the Penrith match, while Joe Roddy returns to the bench. Sebastian Kris is unavailable, forcing another adjustment to the outside backs.
The Raiders’ challenge is avoiding the defensive collapses that have appeared too frequently this season. They have conceded 512 points and average approximately 25.5 points against per game, which places enormous pressure on a young spine to keep producing.
Knights Make Finals Statement at Suncorp
Newcastle’s 30-6 victory over Brisbane was among their most complete performances of the season. The Knights scored five tries, held the Broncos to a single score and effectively ended Brisbane’s already faint finals hopes.
Fletcher Sharpe and Greg Marzhew both scored doubles, while Kalyn Ponga controlled the backfield and repeatedly created attacking opportunities. The result strengthened Newcastle’s position inside the top eight and gave them confidence before another difficult road trip.
The Knights’ spine is the primary reason I rate them above Canberra. Ponga remains the most influential player in the matchup, Sandon Smith gives Newcastle a genuine organising half and Sharpe provides another creative option close to the line.
Bradman Best and Dane Gagai give the Knights power and experience in the centres, while Dominic Young and Marzhew provide elite finishing and yardage from the wings. C

Newcastle’s hopes of cementing their spot inside the NRL’s top eight have been dealt a huge blow with star centre Bradman Best ruled out with a calf injury.
The Knights have had to count the cost of a rousing 30-6 victory over Brisbane last round, as Best emerged from the clash with a low-grade calf strain.
The NSW State of Origin representative’s injury will be unwelcome for Newcastle (12-8), who sit just two points clear of ninth place and are looking to win prop Tyson Frizell’s 300th match on Sunday at GIO Stadium.
Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today Arrow
Best’s niggle is the latest setback in a stop-start campaign as he’s also battled through groin and calf injuries earlier in the season. Fletcher Hunt will shift into the centres while teenager Toby Winter moves onto the bench.
Newcastle’s news comes after Canberra coach Ricky Stuart said their hopes of victory will rest on halfback Ethan Sanders’ kicking game.
The Raiders (9-11) must snare a victory on Sunday if they are to have any chance of securing a winning record and staying in contention for the NRL finals.
However, the weather is set to cause chaos with torrential rain expected to impact the playing surface.
It means the 11th-placed Canberra’s usual razzle dazzle, hard running and fast game will have to be tweaked, and Stuart is relying on Sanders to pick up some of the extra work.
After a rocky start to the year, the young halfback has begun to find his groove with his booming kicks becoming crucial to the Green Machine’s winning formula.
“It (kicking game) is important in every game, but when you’re playing in wet, slippery conditions it is important,” Stuart said.
“You’re going to play a little bit of a different style of game, but we’ve seen the forecast.
“It was meant to be very windy and now it’s probably forecasted not as much wind, but it’s going to be wet here.”
The Raiders welcome back centre Simi Sasagi from a hamstring strain as they look to rebound from a dismal 42-18 loss to Penrith last Saturday.
Along with Sasagi, second-rower Joe Roddy is poised to play his first game off the bench since he broke his hand in round nine and underwent surgery.
“Then last week, there was something wrong with his ankle or whatnot,” Stuart said.
“It’s been disappointing that he hasn’t got more game time this year because it’s what’s needed for him at this stage of his career.

Raiders v Knights: Sasagi returns; Frizell the milestone man
The Raiders will be looking to get back on track this week against the Knights after their recent run of good form was halted by Penrith.
Canberra were aiming for five wins in a row - but against this year's ladder leaders, they hit a snag and were unable to match them in their match at Mudgee.
They face a tough challenge this week however against a Knights side who are still full of belief, despite losing key players Dylan Brown and Dylan Lucas for the season.
Under coach Justin Holbrook this year, Newcastle's team have been rewarded for their spirit and will be looking to press their case for a top four finish with a win.
Last week they proved too strong for the Broncos and ended last year's defending premiers title defence.
In the absence of some of their stars, they have seen some new talents emerge, including forwards Cody Hopwood and Francis Manuleleua.

Team News

Sasagi was a late withdrawal from last week's loss to the Panthers. Back-rower Matty Nicholson has now had two games back off the bench and is part of the interchange again with Stuart indicating he will play NSW Cup later on Sunday if he doesn't get on in NRL. The Raiders have won four of their last five games on their home patch at GIO Stadium. No changes in Saturday's 24-hour update.
Knights: A blow for the Knights on Saturday with Bradman Best dropping out with a calf strain suffered in last week's win over Brisbane. Fletcher Hunt comes into the starting side at centre, with Toby Winter moving onto the six-man bench. After coming off the interchange in 17 of his 18 games this season, veteran Tyson Frizell has been named to start in his 300th NRL match. That pushes Cody Hopwood to the bench. Harrison Graham has been added to the bench after missing last week's game with hamstring tightness.
